review: 1:1–1:2 the Arabic يَا مُنَجِّي يَا مُنَجِّي … أَنْتَ سُلْوَانِي repeats the vocative and then names consolation; the Hebrew keeps the doubled הוֹי מוֹשִׁיעִי and נֶחָמָתִי, since the repetition is the stanza's rocking rhythm, not an overflow.

1:4–2:1 חֻלְשַׁת אֱמוּנָתִי … חֶסֶד יִמְצָא — the Arabic ضَعْفَ إِيمَانِي / سَائِلٌ نُعْمَاكَ يَلْقَى uses 'weakness' and 'finds'; the Hebrew keeps חֻלְשָׁה (the glossary term for weakness, from חֻלְשָׁה in Ps 77:11) and the seeker-finds verb of Jer 29:13.

3:2–3:4 פָּנֶיךָ הַבְּהִירִים … תַּאֲוַת נְפָשׁוֹת — the Arabic وَجْهُكَ الْوَضَّاح … مُنْيَةَ الْأَرْوَاح is 'Your radiant face … the desire of souls'; the Hebrew keeps פָּנִים as the object of the longing (as in Ps 27:8, לְךָ אָמַר לִבִּי בַּקְּשׁוּ פָנָי) rather than a general 'presence'.

4:2–4:3 מְקוֹר כָּל־הַחֲסָדִים … טוֹב חֶלְקִי — the Arabic مَنْبَعُ الْأَلْطَافِ … خَيْرُ نَصِيبٍ is 'fount of graces … best portion'; the Hebrew keeps חֵלֶק in the psalm's sense of the assigned portion (Ps 16:5, מְנָת־חֶלְקִי), so the line is the believer's lot, not merely a preference.

4:4 הָאֳפָיִם — the Arabic الْأَوْصَاف is 'traits/attributes'; the Hebrew uses אֳפָיִם (Job 41:4, 'his features') rather than the later תְּכוּנוֹת, keeping the rare biblical noun for the splendour of His character.
